key_insight: System 1 models made fast, probability-based decisions but performed better on medical knowledge and text understanding than on clinical judgement or imaging.
clinical_relevance: These models may support narrowly defined fixed-choice tasks, but the results do not establish readiness for autonomous clinical use.
method: Evaluated four models zero-shot on 86 public tasks across 14 clinical domains and 20 languages.
Grouped tasks into six capability tiers, with AUROC as the primary outcome.
Assessed calibration, language effects, speed and comparisons with published results and generative models.
evidence_signal: Across 179,111 cases, mean AUROC for the best model per task ranged from 0.94 for medical knowledge to 0.69 for volumetric findings; imaging scored 0.09 below text.
watch_item: Performance varied substantially by task and language: triage nurses outperformed the best model, and accuracy fell by up to 39 percentage points from English to Yoruba.
paper_title: The Value of System 1 Models in Medicine
